description: "Base R legends: position by coordinates or keyword, ncol and horiz layout, titles, the legend box, text styling and justification, and custom legend text."

# Legends {#legend}

## Introduction

In this chapter, we will learn how to:

- position the legend within the plot
- modify the layout using `ncol` and `horiz` arguments
- add title using the `title` set of arguments
- modify the appearance and position of the legend box
- modify the appearance of the text in the legend box

Legends convey information about the data represented by a plot. To understand their importance, let us look at the two plots below. In the first, would you be able to understand what the lines represent without a legend? Maybe yes, but only if the author provides that information as text outside the plot. Such information is useful, but it is also very inconvenient. Now look at the second plot: from the legend at the top right, we can easily interpret what the lines represent. Would you agree that a legend is integral to a plot that represents multiple data series? If yes, let us go ahead and learn how to add a legend to different plots.

Since we have looked at a line graph in the example above, we will learn how to add a legend to a line graph, then generalise the steps to other plots. 

## Data

Let us build a line graph that represents annual economic growth (GDP) data of the BRICS nations for the years 2010-14.

> The values below are a frozen teaching vintage, also shipped as `data/brics-gdp-2010-14.csv`. They differ slightly from the World Bank's current revised series, so treat them as illustrative, not citable statistics.

```{r}
year <- seq(2010, 2014, 1)
india <- c(10.3, 6.6, 5.6, 6.6, 7.2)
china <- c(10.6, 9.5, 7.8, 7.7, 7.3)
russia <- c(4.5, 4.3, 3.5, 1.3, 0.7)
brazil <- c(7.5, 3.9, 1.9, 3.0, 0.1)
s_africa <- c(3.2, 3.2, 2.2, 2.2, 1.5)
gdp <- data.frame(year, india, china, russia, brazil, s_africa, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
gdp
```

## Line Graph

Below is the line graph that represents the above GDP data set:

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.width= 7, fig.height=7, echo=FALSE}
#| label: fig-legend-motivate
#| fig-cap: "The problem a legend solves: five series with nothing to tell them apart"
#| fig-alt: "A line chart of five economic growth series for the BRICS countries between 2010 and 2014. The lines cross repeatedly and none is labelled, so there is no way to tell which line represents which country. One series falls steeply to near zero by 2014 and another falls almost to zero."
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$russia, col = 'green')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$brazil, col = 'yellow')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$s_africa, col = 'violet')}
```

Without a legend, it is very difficult to map the lines to the BRICS nations. We will add a legend to the plot above using the `legend()` function, one step at a time.

## Legend Location

To add a legend to the plot, the first thing we must specify is its location. There are 2 ways to do this:

- use x and y axis coordinates
- use keywords

The list of keywords include:

- top
- bottom
- left
- right
- center
- bottomright
- bottomleft
- topright
- topleft

But there is a glitch: if we do not specify what goes into the legend, the `legend()` function returns an error. Before we experiment with the location, we need to learn about another argument that specifies the content of the legend. The argument is also named `legend`, and it takes a vector as input. In the next example, we plot the GDP data for India and China and add a basic legend.

```{r leg1, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2013, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'))}
```

You can see that a legend has been added based on the X and Y axis coordinates we specified in the `legend()` function. But the legend is incomplete: a user still cannot map the lines to the countries. We will learn how to add lines inside the legend shortly, but first let us use keywords to position it inside the plot. 

```{r leg2, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=15, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(3, 3))
values <- c('top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'center',
            'bottomright', 'bottomleft', 'topright', 'topleft')
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  legend(x = i, legend = c('india', 'china'))
  mtext(paste("x = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

You can use either the keywords or the axis coordinates to position the legend inside the plot. Use the coordinates method if you want greater control over its position. The next step is to add lines inside the legend so that a user can map the lines to the countries.

## Lines

Adding a line to the legend is very simple. Use the `lty` argument to specify the line type and the `col` argument to add color. 

```{r leg3, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'))}
```

Now we can map the lines to the respective countries using the legend. But our legend looks very simple. Let us explore the options available to modify and enhance the appearance of the legend.

## Points

If the plot has both lines and points, we can use the `pch` argument in the `legend()` function to specify the shape of the point.

```{r leg4, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
points(gdp$year, gdp$india, pch = 2, col = 'blue')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
points(gdp$year, gdp$china, pch = 2, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, pch = 2, col = c('blue', 'red'))}
```

## Text Placement

We can position the contents of the legend horizontally using the `horiz` argument. It takes logical values as input, and the default is `FALSE`. Set it to `TRUE` to position the contents horizontally:

```{r leg5, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2011, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'),
       horiz = TRUE)}
```

Another way to position the content inside the legend is to use columns. In the example below, we use the `ncol` argument to split the contents into two columns instead of the default one. 


```{r leg6, fig.align='center', fig.width= 7, fig.height=7, echo=FALSE}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$russia, col = 'green')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$brazil, col = 'yellow')
legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china', 'russia', 'brazil'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red', 'green', 'yellow'),
       ncol = 2)}
```

The plots below show the difference in appearance:

```{r leg7, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
values <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$russia, col = 'green')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$brazil, col = 'yellow')
  legend(x = 2010, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china', 'russia','brazil'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red', 'green', 'yellow'),
       ncol = i)
  mtext(paste("ncol = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Title

Let us add a title to the legend using the `title` argument:

```{r leg8, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'),
       title = 'Nations')}
```

### Title Color

The color of the title can be modified using the `title.col` argument:

```{r leg9, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 14, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'),
       title = 'Nations', title.col = 'red')}
```

### Title Position

We can position the title within the legend box using the `title.adj` argument. It takes values between 0 and 1. The default is 0.5, which places the title in the middle of the box. As the value moves away from 0.5, the title moves to the left or the right.

```{r leg10, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), horiz = TRUE,
       title = 'Nations', title.adj = 0.1)}
```

The plots below show the relative position of the title within the legend box for different values between 0 and 1.

```{r leg11, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
values <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  legend(x = 2010, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), horiz = TRUE,
       title = 'Nations', title.adj = i)
  mtext(paste("title.adj = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Box Appearance

There are many options to modify the appearance of the legend box. The table below displays the arguments and their descriptions. Let us look at them one by one:

```{r kable, echo=FALSE}
option <- c('Box Type', 'Background Color', 'Border Line Type',
            'Border Line Width', 'Border Line Color', 
            'Horizontal Justification', 'Vertical Justification',
            'Text Color', 'Text Font')
argument <- c('bty', 'bg', 'box.lty', 'box.lwd', 'box.col',
              'xjust', 'yjust', 'text.col', 'text.font')
values <- c('o, n', 'blue, #0000ff', '1:5', '0.5, 1, 1.5',
            'blue, #0000ff', '0:1', '0:1', 'blue, #0000ff',
            '1:5')
legend <- data.frame(option, argument, values)
knitr::kable(legend, format = "markdown", caption = "Legend Box Options")
```

### Box Type

The `bty` argument takes two values, `o` and `n`. If set to `n`, no box is drawn around the legend.

```{r leg12, fig.align='center', fig.width=10, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
values <- c('o', 'n')
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), bty = i,
       title = 'Nations')
  mtext(paste("bty = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

### Background Color

We can add a background color to the legend box using the `bg` argument:

```{r leg13, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), title = 'Nations',
       bg = 'lightyellow')
```

### Border

We can modify the border of the legend box with the following arguments:

- `box.lty`: line type
- `box.lwd`: line width
- `box.col`: color

```{r leg14, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), title = 'Nations',
       box.lty = 3, box.lwd = 1.5, box.col = 'green')
```

## Justification

We can use the `xjust` and `yjust` arguments to position the legend relative to the **X** and **Y** axis respectively. Below are the values and the justification each gives:

- `0`: left justified
- `0.5`: centered
- `1`: right justified

Let us look at a few examples to understand how it works.

### Horizontal Justification

```{r leg15, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
values <- c(0, 0.5, 1)
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), xjust = i,
       title = 'Nations')
  mtext(paste("xjust = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

### Vertical Justification

```{r leg16, fig.align='center', fig.width=15, fig.height=5, echo=FALSE}
init <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
values <- c(0, 0.5, 1)
for (i in values) {
  plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
  lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
  legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), yjust = i,
       title = 'Nations')
  mtext(paste("yjust = ", i), side = 3, col = "blue")
}
par(init)
```

## Text Appearance

The last topic we will explore is the appearance of the text inside the legend box. We will modify the color and font of the text using the `text.col` and `text.font` arguments.

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
#| label: fig-legend-final
#| fig-cap: "A complete legend with a title, styled keys and horizontal layout"
#| fig-alt: "The same five-series growth chart, now with a legend in the top left corner. The legend has a title and a bordered box, and each entry pairs a short coloured line segment with the country name it identifies."
{plot(gdp$year, gdp$india, type = 'l',
      ylim = c(-5, 15), xlab = 'Year',
      ylab = 'Growth Rate', col = 'blue',
      main = 'BRICS: Growth Rate')
lines(gdp$year, gdp$china, col = 'red')
legend(x = 2012, y = 0, legend = c('india', 'china'),
       lty = 1, col = c('blue', 'red'), title = 'Nations',
       text.col = 'green', text.font = 3)}
```
